problem:
A function $g(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| **$x$** | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(x)$ | $-5.0$ | $-4.0$ | $-2.7$ | $-1.0$ | $0.5$ |

$$

$$

Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a central difference approximation.

${g}^{′}(-1)≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=-1.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{g(-1+1)-g(-1-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{g(0)-g(-2)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{-1.0-(-4.0)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$
